children: The maker of Mucinex and Lysol is doubling down on U.S. product development and manufacturing to respond more quickly to shifts in consumer demand.
Consumer-goods seller Reckitt Benckiser Group said Wednesday it plans to invest about $400 million over the next four years in the U.S., building on a $200 million commitment made in 2024.
The additional investment is meant to speed up product innovation, help bolster its supply chain against disruptions and speed up its ability to meet spikes in consumer demand.

"We're investing now to support the next phase of growth for our U.S. business, which remains a key market for us and one where we see strong long-term potential," said Jérôme Lemaire, president of North America for U.K.-based Reckitt.

Reckitt has been investing in the U.S. to get new products to customers faster and meet fluctuating drug demand as the timing of each year's cold and flu season shifts. The company bought a factory in Wilson, N.C., in 2024 to move some production of Mucinex cough and cold medicines from factories in Mexico and the U.K. to the U.S.
It now plans to double its investment in that plant to $400 million, including adding 234,000 square feet to the 310,000-square-foot building.

Under the plan, the Wilson factory will become Reckitt's largest over-the-counter manufacturing facility in the U.S. and will grow its production capacity for Mucinex tablets and liquids, as well as its Move Free joint-health supplement. The new facility will allow the company to make more than 80% of its Mucinex products in the U.S.

Reckitt is also working to consolidate its commercial and research-and-development operations onto one campus in Nutley, N.J. In January, the company moved its North American headquarters about 15 miles east to Nutley from Parsippany.

It now plans to move its research and development teams focused on germ-killing products such as Lysol to that campus from nearby Montvale. Reckitt plans to build a science-and-innovation center adjacent to its headquarters, with the goal of speeding up the product development process to get new items onto store shelves faster.

North American sales made up about 23% of Reckitt's core net revenue in the first half of this year, compared with 33% of revenue from Europe and 44% from emerging markets such as China, India and Brazil.

More companies have sought to brace their supply chains against disruptions such as extreme weather, shipping delays and factory shutdowns since the Covid-19 pandemic, including by manufacturing goods closer to consumers. The Trump administration has also pushed for businesses to manufacture more goods in the U.S., including by imposing hefty tariffs on imports.

"Having plants throughout the world allows [companies] to respond more rapidly to more localized or regional needs than just having one base in one country," said Justin Kistler, a supply-chain management professor at the University of Tennessee.

For example, if cold and flu season "arrives three, four weeks earlier in the U.S. this year than it did in prior years, if we're only solely producing in Europe, getting that product produced and then onto a ship, we miss the boat," Kistler said. "Our competitors beat us to it in terms of product availability."
